glossary: M endorsement
The motorcycle class added to a US driver licence after a written and road test, or an MSF rider course. No engine-size ladder for adults: pass once and any bike is legal.
Autocycle

Three-wheelers such as the Polaris Slingshot are "autocycles" in about 45 states (a car licence is enough); Can-Am Spyder and Ryker and Harley trikes count as motorcycles in many states and need the M endorsement.
DCT / E-Clutch
Honda’s dual-clutch automatic (no clutch lever) and its E-Clutch, which works the clutch for you while you still shift gears. Twist-and-go scooters use a CVT instead.
Helmet laws
Universal helmet laws in 19 states plus DC; most other states require helmets under 18 or 21; Illinois, Iowa and New Hampshire have none.

Boater education card

No federal licence, but almost every state requires a safety course for operators born after a cut-off year (Florida 1988, Texas 1993, Georgia 1998) or for everyone (California, New York). Online NASBLA courses cost $0–$60.
USCG documentation
Optional federal registration for boats of 5 net tons and over (roughly 27 ft up): about $133 to start and $26 a year; lenders often require it above $50,000.

Since 2021 federal law requires the lanyard on planing boats under 26 ft; on a PWC it must be worn at all times.

Massachusetts charges $10 per $1,000 of value a year; Connecticut, Maine, South Carolina, Virginia, Missouri and Kansas levy personal-property tax on boats. Shown as information, not added.

glossary: Factory list vs typically equipped
Makers quote a base price and a "typically equipped" price with the options most buyers take; the row’s range spans both.
Delivery position
New aircraft are sold as positions in the production line; a hot type means a wait of one to three years, and positions trade at a premium.
Pre-buy / acceptance inspection
An independent inspection before you accept delivery, even on a new aircraft; catches squawks the factory should fix at its cost.
Registration
Every aircraft is registered with the national authority (FAA N-number, CAA G-register, EASA state registers, DGCA VT-, CAAC B-); the fee is small, the paperwork is not.
Owner-flown
Aircraft a licensed private pilot can fly without a professional crew: pistons, most turboprops and a few single-pilot jets (Vision Jet, Citation M2, Phenom 100).
eVTOL

Electric vertical take-off aircraft; the EHang EH216-S is certified in China and ultralight single-seaters fly in the US, while the air-taxi designs (Joby, Archer, VX4) are still in certification and not sold to individuals.
LSA / MOSAIC
Light-sport aircraft: simple two-seaters flown on a sport-pilot licence; the FAA’s 2025 MOSAIC rule lets heavier four-seaters qualify.
TBO
Time between overhauls of the engine, 1,500 to 2,200 hours on pistons; an overhaul costs US$30,000 to US$60,000 and is part of the running cost.
Fly-away exemption
Texas, Florida, Kansas and others exempt a sale from sales tax when the buyer flies the aircraft out of the state within a set number of days; your home state may then charge use tax.
